findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC8 with ADR 0059's measured Opus-on-Bedrock silent no-caching: either scope the 'caching confirmed active' AC to the Sonnet (Tier-1) tier only and state explicitly that Opus Tier-2 runs are billed uncached (revising the ~$3.4/review basis and the $200/$30 budget accordingly), or add a SPIKE to first verify whether claude-opus-4-8 caches on the configured Bedrock region/profile before committing the Tier-2 baseline spend.
evidence: Plan AC8: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call of a run); verified from the usage log.'
Plan invariant 2: 'frontier Opus for Pass 1 … through Bedrock only'; the production Opus id is claude-opus-4-8 (docs/ci-provider-matrix.md:112).

docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md:560-565 (MEASURED): 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-… AND global.anthropic.… both returned cache_read=0 and cache_write=0 on both attempts with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning … This silent double-billing is the real hazard.'

The only Bedrock run with nonzero cache counters (docs/ci-provider-matrix.md:117-119) is a MIXED 19×opus-4-8 + 9×sonnet-4-6 + 1×haiku run whose cache read/write is aggregated across all calls (Sonnet caches), so it does not establish Opus-4-8 caching on Bedrock.
ADR 0059 stresses caching is MODEL-dependent and the discriminator is the model, not the profile prefix — so Sonnet caching on Bedrock does not generalize to Opus.
findings.finding: AC8 asserts prompt caching will be 'confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call)', but for the Tier-2 pass the plan mandates frontier Opus via Bedrock only (invariant 2), and ADR 0059's own measured facts show Opus on Bedrock returns cache_read=0/cache_write=0 silently — the asserted caching capability is contradicted/unverified for the plan's own frontier tier.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs …'; Approach — Tier 2 (Opus … ~$3.4/review uncached); Invariants 1–2
scenarios: The Tier-2 baseline sample (~20 tickets, Opus via Bedrock) runs; the second call shows cache_read_tokens=0, so AC8's confirmation can never pass for the Opus tier — or the run silently double-bills full input on every call and blows the commissioning-spend estimate.

The $200 hard budget / $30 reserve is planned against a ~$3.4/review 'uncached' Tier-2 figure that implicitly assumes some caching benefit; if Opus never caches on Bedrock, actual Tier-2 spend is materially higher than budgeted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate AC#1 to verify against what material_fingerprint actually attests (the canonicalized material BASIS — description/file_impact/children, checkbox+whitespace-normalized), drop or qualify the 'byte-exact' claim, and state how non-material or box-state/whitespace-only reconstruction differences are handled (e.g. reconstruct to canonical form and verify the basis, accepting these are normalized out).
evidence: Plan: 'The reviewed plan text is not stored but is reconstructable … and verifiable byte-exactly against the stored material_fingerprint.'

pass1.material_fingerprint / material_diff.material_basis: the fingerprint hashes ONLY {ticket_id, canonical_description, file_impact, children[, file_impact_scope]}, with checkbox STATE and insignificant whitespace normalized away (normalize_checkbox_state, normalize_insignificant_whitespace), truncated to sha256[:16].
So two reconstructions differing only in box state or trailing whitespace produce an IDENTICAL fingerprint — 'byte-exact' is unprovable from it; and material excludes tags/comments/links entirely.
findings.finding: AC#1 claims at-review plan text is 'verifiable byte-exactly against the stored material_fingerprint', but material_fingerprint hashes only a CANONICALIZED material basis, so it cannot verify byte-exactness and the stated verification mechanism does not hold as written.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, bullet 1 ('at-review plan text reconstructed and fingerprint-verified byte-exactly … for ≥95% of v2 sidecars'); Context para 3
scenarios: A reconstruction that restores canonical description but not the exact box-tick sequence or trailing whitespace present at review time 'verifies' — silently feeding Tier-1 a plan text that is NOT what the production reviewer saw.
A ticket whose review-time text differed only in a non-material field is treated as reconstructed when it was not.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC#1 to: 'at-review plan MATERIAL (description/file_impact/decomposition) reconstructed to canonical form and its material_fingerprint matched byte-for-byte against the stored value for ≥95% of v2 sidecars', and note that checkbox state / insignificant whitespace / non-material fields are normalized out of the fingerprint and therefore out of scope for the match.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Establish (or spike) that at-review description text is recoverable for the target tickets under SNAPSHOT compaction — confirm retired EDIT event files are retained in origin/tickets git history and reconstructable at the review timestamp — before committing to the ≥95% reconstruction bar.
evidence: event-schema.md, SNAPSHOT row: 'Folds prior replay state into one compiled-state event … Compaction renames folded files with the *.retired suffix.'

EDIT reduces by 'Replay order selects the last value for each edited field' — only the COMPILED latest description survives a SNAPSHOT-only replay; earlier at-review description text lives only in the retired EDIT event files.
Plan concedes ~2,000 sidecars are 'pruned from the tree but recoverable from origin/tickets history' — recoverability of the corresponding retired EDIT bodies is asserted, not demonstrated.
findings.finding: The ≥95% plan-text reconstruction target assumes historical description versions are recoverable from EDIT/SNAPSHOT history, but SNAPSHOT compaction folds prior replay state and retires the source EDIT files, so intermediate at-review descriptions may be irrecoverable; the plan asserts git recoverability without establishing that the specific retired EDITs survive.
findings.location: Context para 3 ('reconstructable from ticket EDIT/SNAPSHOT history'; '~2,000 older ones pruned … recoverable from origin/tickets history'); AC#1
scenarios: A ticket reviewed at description v3, later edited to v5 and then compacted: the v3 EDIT is retired/folded; if that retired file was not retained in origin/tickets git history, the at-review text cannot be reconstructed and the sidecar fails the fingerprint match.
A large share of the ~2,000 git-recovered sidecars turn out to lack their at-review EDIT body, dropping reconstruction below the 95% bar after the corpus build is already committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scoping step to the corpus-builder child that (a) enumerates which sidecars require pre-snapshot EDIT bodies, (b) confirms those retired files exist in origin/tickets, and (c) reports the achievable reconstruction rate; make AC#1's threshold conditional on that measured ceiling rather than a fixed 95%.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'friction rate' in the plan: numerator, denominator, and aggregation unit.
evidence: AC3 lists 'friction rate' as a diff-report output with no definition anywhere in the plan
E2 data-design rule: a derived metric with no computation or aggregation protocol is an ambiguity under signals (1)/(2)
findings.finding: 'friction rate' is reported as a Tier-0 metric but its computation/aggregation is never defined.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, Tier-0 bullet ('...label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate')
scenarios: Executor building the Tier-0 report must guess what 'friction rate' counts (e.g. revise-triggering blocks per review? per ticket?) before proceeding.
findings.suggested_fix: State e.g. 'friction rate = fraction of reviews whose verdict is BLOCK/revise, per corpus, computed over the frozen corpus.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the label-proxy: which label sources define positives/negatives and how a stored verdict maps to a predicted class for precision/recall.
evidence: Context enumerates label sources (2,483 revise pairs, 84 plan_defect, 199 PASS->FAIL, etc.) but AC3 asks for 'label-proxy precision/recall' without specifying which labels are the ground-truth positives/negatives or how a review's verdict maps to a prediction
findings.finding: The 'label-proxy precision/recall' metric has no stated mapping from the enumerated label sources to a precision/recall computation.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (Tier-0), Approach / Context labels list
scenarios: Executor cannot compute precision/recall without deciding which labels count as true-positive plan defects vs false alarms — a load-bearing design choice left open.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the stratification dimensions for the fixed sample (e.g. stratify by stored verdict and by outcome-label presence).
evidence: 'a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)' — no strata named (by verdict? criterion mix? outcome label? store?)
E2 signal (1)/(2): the selection protocol is a real design choice deferred to the executor
findings.finding: The stratified sample (~20 tickets) is specified by size but not by stratification dimensions.
findings.location: Approach, Tier-2 bullet; AC5 ('fixed stratified sample')
scenarios: Executor must invent the stratification axes; a non-representative sample would bias every Tier-2 measurement built on it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default disposition of sidecars whose plan text fails fingerprint verification (e.g. 'excluded from Tier-1/2 eligibility, retained for Tier-0 which needs no plan text').
evidence: 'at-review plan text reconstructed and fingerprint-verified for ≥95% of v2 sidecars' — the disposition of the unverifiable remainder is unstated (excluded from Tier-1/2? included for Tier-0 only?)
findings.finding: The plan requires fingerprint-verified reconstruction for '≥95% of v2 sidecars' but does not state how the remaining <5% (failed reconstruction) are handled in the corpus.
scenarios: Tier-1/Tier-2 replay needs plan text; a sidecar whose text fails fingerprint verification cannot be replayed — is it dropped, or replayed with unverified text?
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Sidecars failing fingerprint verification are marked text_unverified and excluded from Tier-1/2 sampling; they remain in the Tier-0 corpus.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short prior-art / build-vs-adopt subsection that names the relevant external eval frameworks (e.g. promptfoo, DeepEval, OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, Braintrust) and justifies why the sidecar-replay CORE must be bespoke (internal review_kernel coupling, byte-exact material_fingerprint replay, production model-parity) while explaining whether the GENERIC scaffolding — cost ledger/budget pre-flight, model routing, regression diff/report — is reused from or deliberately diverges from one of these tools.
evidence: The plan grounds novelty ENTIRELY in internal prior art (ADR 0054, epic 6982, docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py, docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py) and names no external framework anywhere.

Retrieved (promptfoo/promptfoo GitHub; aitestingguide.com Promptfoo review 2026, retrieved this run): promptfoo is a widely-used prompt/agent testing tool that supports 'prompt regression testing (ensuring prompt changes do not break existing behaviour), multi-model benchmarking … cost-per-run validation, and golden dataset comparison', with custom API providers and CI/CD integration; the same source names DeepEval, OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, and Braintrust as established alternatives — i.e. the ledger/budget-preflight, model-routing, and regression-diff scaffolding this plan builds from scratch is a well-trodden external pattern.

Retrieved (fullstackpm.tech 'LLM Prompt Evaluation Framework', retrieved this run) describes the identical pipeline this plan reinvents: 'LLM-as-Judge scores output against rubric → Store results → Compare Versions (v1 vs v2) → Detect Regressions (flag score drops).'

ABSENCE: the plan makes an implicit novel-architecture claim (a purpose-built harness package under src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/) but performs no anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three check against these existing tools for the generic layers.
findings.finding: The plan commits to a fully bespoke eval/prompt-regression harness (cost ledger with budget pre-flight, prompt-caching confirmation, per-run model-parity guard, noise-band regression acceptance, versioned corpus + diff/report artifacts) without any consideration of the mature external prior-art class that provides exactly these generic capabilities off the shelf.
findings.location: Approach / Scope / Acceptance Criteria (the generic harness scaffolding — ledger, model-parity guard, report/diff, corpus versioning)
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why rebar hand-rolls a cost ledger + model-parity guard + regression-report format that promptfoo/DeepEval already provide, and finds no recorded build-vs-adopt rationale.
The bespoke ledger/report format diverges from an industry-standard eval schema, raising long-term maintenance cost with no documented justification for the divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, add: 'Prior art: external LLM-eval frameworks (promptfoo, DeepEval, OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, Braintrust) provide prompt-regression testing, golden-dataset comparison, multi-model benchmarking, and cost-per-run validation. They are rejected for the replay CORE because it must re-execute the exact production review_kernel seams (pass3_decide, verify_findings) against internally-stored plan_review_result_v2 sidecars with byte-exact material_fingerprint verification and per-pass Bedrock model parity — coupling no external tool models. For the generic scaffolding (cost ledger, model-parity guard, diff/report), we [reuse promptfoo's provider/cost layer | deliberately hand-roll because <reason>].'
